newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: SENATE TO VOTE ON COLSTON PROPOSAL
The Senate's expected to vote on a proposal to make public all travel allowance documents of all Senators.
The Federal Opposition and Australian Democrats say they'll support the proposal by Independent Senator Mal Colston.
The Senate is also expected to vote on a move to pursue Senator Colston's possible mis-use of travel allowance.
Senator Colston says as his travel allowance claims have received detailed scrutiny, the same should apply to every other member of the Senate, for the past five years.
The Opposition says it's happy to comply with full disclosure and has nothing to hide, and the Democrats will also support it.
Coalition Senators met last night to decide their position, but would not comment.
INSTITUTE WARNS OF RECESSION
The National Insitute of Economic and Industry Research says the Reserve Bank should increase interest rates, because low interest rates are leading to unsustainable consumer borrowing and spending.
The Insititute says whilst the economy is set for a substantial period of economic growth, this will have ended by 2001.
It has warned Australia could plunge into the worst recesssion since the Second World War.
Executive Director Dr Peter Brain says the result of low interest rates will result in, when interest rates rise, people being forced to cut back expenditure sharply, triggering the recession.
Dr Brain also says the Federal Government must look at radical tax reform through a GST.
UNION SAYS 500 ESANDA JOBS ON CHOPPING BLOCK
Staff of Esanda Finance Corporation will meet around the country today to discuss plans by the company to centralise some operations, and make large-scale job cuts.
The Finance Sector Union says about 500 jobs will go across the corporation, an arm of the ANZ group.
The meetings will discuss company plans to centralise much of its data processing operations in Melbourne.
Union official, Grahame Pine, says about 50 new jobs would be created in Victoria.
Esanda says new technology and increasing competition have led to the need for the cuts.
It says a period of rapid global transformation means the changes are needed so that Esanda can compete against bank and non-bank lenders.
DEPUTY PM TABLES LETTER IN PARLIAMENT
Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer says he'll continue to defend his right to debate the judgements of the High Court.
Late last year Mr Fischer criticised the Court's tardiness in handing down its Wik ruling on native title and pastoral leases.
The Chief Justice of the High Court, Sir Gerard Brennan, wrote to Mr Fischer in January, saying the criticism was unjustified, adding that such attacks were damaging to the Court.
Mr Fischer replied in the same month, acknowledging his comments were based on incorrect advice.
Responding to a question from the Opposition, Mr Fischer has tabled the letter in Parliament.
The Opposition says Mr Fischer should have corrected the public record earlier.
VIOLENCE CONTINUES IN ALBANIA
In the eastern European country of Albania, violent anti-government protests over the collapse of pyramid investment schemes are continuing.
Chaos and anarchy reign in the southern town of Vlore, the focus of the riots.
Witnesses in the town say armed men are firing automatic weapons at will.
Thirteen people died in clashes on the weekend.
In the capital, Tirana, at least 20 people have been arrested, and soldiers are patrolling the streets.
A curfew has been been imposed and the army's been ordered to shoot civilians carrying weapons.
Anti-government demonstrators are demanding the resignation of the President Sali Berisha, who's been sworn in for a second five-year term.
TRIAL BEGINS OF TJANDAMURRA O'SHANE ACCUSED
A 26-year-old man goes on trial in Cairns today accused of setting fire to six-year-old schoolboy Tjandamurra O'Shane last year.
Paul Wade Streeton faces two charges over the attack - attempted unlawful killing and intent to do grevious bodily harm.
Tjandamurra O'Shane has had nine skin grafts since being doused with petrol and set alight last year in the grounds of the Cairns North State School.
